newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's fiscal situation improves slightly.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's fiscal situation improves slightly.

text.p: Brazil's public sector fiscal situation improved slightly in January thanks to streamlining efforts by states and municipalities and lower interest payments, said Altamir Lopes, head of the Central Bank's economics department.
"The operational deficit fell for two reasons: the primary result was better and interest payments...were lower," Lopes said.

The consolidated public sector posted an operational deficit equivalent to 3.65 percent of gross domestic product, narrower than December's 3.85 percent of GDP deficit and last January's shortfall of 5.47 percent of GDP, the bank said in a statement.
The public sector's primary result was a 0.01 percent surplus versus a 0.07 percent deficit in December and a 0.34 percent deficit in January 1996.

"The primary result has shown a tendency towards improvement since last June," Lopes told reporters, adding the improvement was not necessarily spectacular but that things were heading in the right direction.

In terms of monthly flows, the federal government's primary result in January was worse than that of a year ago due to high tax receipts, Lopes said. The federal government is only part of the public sector, which includes state and municipal governments and state-owned companies.
The higher tax revenues meant unusually large constitutional transfers to the states, pressuring the federal government's accounts and helping the states to improve their fiscal performance.
Under the Brazilian constitution, the federal government must increase its transfers to the states if it takes in greater revenues.
